summary:
Reuters reporting, republished by Allwork.Space, says Flock Safety plans to cut roughly 18% of its workforce, about 270 employees, following a voluntary buyout program announced in September. The company, which makes AI-powered surveillance cameras and automated license-plate readers, employs about 1,500 people, and affected staff were expected to leave at the end of the month. Flock declined to comment and had not made the plan public; sources spoke anonymously.

The cuts come as Flock faces mounting opposition from communities, regulators, lawmakers and privacy advocates, even while venture investors remain enthusiastic. A Reuters/Ipsos poll found Americans divided, with 38% supporting the use of Flock cameras in their community versus 47% opposed.

Founded in 2017 and based in Atlanta, Flock operates a network of roughly 120,000 AI-powered cameras across 49 states, mounted on streets and highways to automatically read license plates and record passing vehicles. It has raised over $950 million in venture capital, most recently a $275 million round in March led by Andreessen Horowitz at a $7.5 billion valuation. Those funds support a new US manufacturing facility and a planned expansion into drone products. Flock serves more than 4,800 law enforcement agencies and nearly 1,000 businesses.

Scrutiny has intensified around alleged privacy violations and data-sharing practices. In September, Florida banned automated license plate readers from state highways on privacy grounds tied to Flock's cameras. Home Depot investors demanded reviews of the retailer's relationships with surveillance technology vendors after reports that Flock data was used in immigration enforcement. A Virginia privacy lawsuit alleges the widespread camera deployment amounts to warrantless surveillance. Alongside AI data centers, Flock cameras have become a flashpoint in this year's midterm elections, with candidates attacking opponents by linking them to the technology.

Reporting by Krystal Hu and Helen Coster, edited by David Gregorio.
